title: Dunn rank comparisons
biology: Ecologists compare skewed leaf-damage measurements among four treatments.
design: 21 independent leaves from different plants per treatment.
question: Which pairs differ in their rank tendencies?
null: For a chosen pair, pooled-rank tendencies are equal under the common-distribution null.
options: altp = TRUE prints ordinary two-sided p-values
kw = FALSE avoids repeating the omnibus calculation
assumptions: Comparable shapes are needed for a simple location interpretation
parametric: If mean damage is the target, use an appropriate response model
Model scale changes rather than relabeling ranks as mean effects
nonparametric: This is already a rank procedure
A design-valid permutation can use a different prespecified statistic
practice: Can this result be reported as a difference in mean damage?
code_simulate:
set.seed(2105)
d <- data.frame(leaf = 1:84,
                treatment = rep(c("A", "B", "C", "D"), each = 21))
d$damage <- rlnorm(84, rep(c(1.2, 1.3, 1.7, 1.9), each = 21), .48)
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
par(mar = c(5, 5, 2, 1), las = 1, bty = "l", cex = 1.15)
beeswarm::beeswarm(damage ~ treatment, data = d,
  pch = 21, bg = c("#246A73", "#73969B", "#D7A583", "#B7663E"),
  col = "white", cex = 1.25, xlab = "Treatment",
  ylab = "Leaf area removed (mm²)")
points(1:4, tapply(d$damage, d$treatment, median),
       pch = 18, cex = 2, col = "#172D34")
legend("topleft", "Diamonds = sample medians", pch = 18, bty = "n")
code_analysis:
overall <- kruskal.test(damage ~ treatment, data = d)
comparisons <- dunn.test::dunn.test(d$damage, d$treatment,
  method = "holm", altp = TRUE, kw = FALSE, list = FALSE)
generating_model: 21 independent leaves in each of four groups have log-normal damage. Log damage is Normal(mean, 0.48²), with means 1.2, 1.3, 1.7 and 1.9 for A–D. Damage remains positive and unrounded. All leaves come from different plants.
generating_truth: Group distributions differ; their population medians are exp(1.2), exp(1.3), exp(1.7) and exp(1.9) mm². Dunn tests pooled-rank tendencies, not arithmetic mean equality. The distributions also differ in original-scale spread.

columns.name: leaf
columns.meaning: Independent leaf from a distinct plant

teaching_point: After choosing a rank question, retain multiplicity protection for pairwise follow-ups.
